text_simplified: A young girl grows up on acts of goodness when she sees them, becomes accustomed to them and excels in them as she grows: she puts what she can into a charity box to remove stinginess from her soul, hastens to voluntary acts of worship, and makes serving the religion and calling to it her concern—like that female student who was found in the school prayer area at break praying Duha. The author advises opening the door of dialogue with the daughter so parents can know what is in her heart and guide her accordingly, and this strengthens her bond with her family.
